insert.subject: Chemistry
insert.question: Some alkyl halides undergo substitution whereas some undergo elimination on treatment with bases. Which structural feature mainly decides this?
insert.option1: Primary alkyl halides with a strong, unhindered nucleophile mainly give $S_N2$ substitution; tertiary alkyl halides with a strong base mainly give elimination (stable carbocation, crowded carbon)
insert.option2: Primary alkyl halides mainly give elimination while tertiary alkyl halides mainly give $S_N2$ substitution
insert.option3: All alkyl halides give only substitution; elimination occurs only with aryl halides
insert.option4: The size of the halogen alone decides it; the structure of the alkyl group has no role
insert.correct_option: Primary alkyl halides with a strong, unhindered nucleophile mainly give $S_N2$ substitution; tertiary alkyl halides with a strong base mainly give elimination (stable carbocation, crowded carbon)

insert.subject: Chemistry
insert.question: Some halogen compounds are useful in daily life but expose flora and fauna to more UV light by damaging the ozone layer. These compounds and a sensible way to reduce their harmful effects are:
insert.option1: Iodoform; use it only as an antiseptic
insert.option2: DDT; spray it only on crops
insert.option3: Chlorofluorocarbons (freons); replace them by ozone-friendly substitutes and avoid their release into the air
insert.option4: Carbon tetrachloride; use it only in fire extinguishers
insert.correct_option: Chlorofluorocarbons (freons); replace them by ozone-friendly substitutes and avoid their release into the air

insert.subject: Chemistry
insert.question: Aryl halides are less reactive than alkyl halides towards nucleophilic substitution. Which is NOT a reason for this?
insert.option1: Resonance gives the C–X bond partial double bond character
insert.option2: The carbon of the C–X bond is $sp^2$ hybridised, so the bond is shorter and stronger
insert.option3: The phenyl cation formed by $S_N1$ is not stabilised by resonance
insert.option4: The halogen in aryl halides is a poorer leaving group because the C–X bond is more polar
insert.correct_option: The halogen in aryl halides is a poorer leaving group because the C–X bond is more polar

insert.subject: Chemistry
insert.question: The reactivity of aryl halides towards nucleophilic substitution can be increased by:
insert.option1: Electron releasing groups such as $\ce{-CH3}$ at meta position
insert.option2: Electron withdrawing groups such as $\ce{-NO2}$ at ortho and/or para positions
insert.option3: Electron withdrawing groups such as $\ce{-NO2}$ at meta position only
insert.option4: Carrying out the reaction at room temperature
insert.correct_option: Electron withdrawing groups such as $\ce{-NO2}$ at ortho and/or para positions
